stem: The hypoglossal nerve innervates all of the following muscles EXCEPT for the:
fact: CN XII supplies the intrinsic and extrinsic muscles of the tongue except palatoglossus, which is supplied by the vagus nerve.
mnemonic: XII moves the tongue; X supplies palatoglossus.
finding: Source page displays palatoglossus as the exception.

stem: Regarding the trigeminal nerve, which of the following statements is INCORRECT:
options: The trigeminal nerve is the largest cranial nerve.
The trigeminal nerve has both motor and sensory function.
The trigeminal nerve is the afferent nerve for the corneal blink reflex.
All three divisions of the trigeminal nerve have bilateral cortical representation.
In a trigeminal nerve palsy, the jaw will deviate away from the affected side when open.
fact: In a trigeminal motor palsy, the jaw deviates toward the affected side on opening because the opposite lateral pterygoid acts unopposed.
mnemonic: Jaw deviates toward the weak pterygoid side.
finding: Source page displays the away-from-affected-side statement as incorrect.

stem: The mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve exits the skull through the:
fact: The mandibular division, V3, exits the skull through the foramen ovale.
mnemonic: V2 uses rotundum; V3 uses ovale.
finding: Source page displays foramen ovale as correct.

stem: The auriculotemporal nerve carries general sensation from all of the following regions EXCEPT for the:
fact: The auriculotemporal nerve supplies the temple, external ear, external auditory canal, outer tympanic membrane, and TMJ, not the upper lip.
mnemonic: Auriculotemporal covers ear, temple, drum, and TMJ; V2 covers the upper lip.
finding: Source page displays upper lip as the exception.

stem: Regarding the optic nerve, which of the following statements is CORRECT:
options: The optic nerve is surrounded by the cranial meninges.
The optic nerve leaves the orbit through the superior orbital fissure.
The optic nerve has both motor and sensory function.
The optic nerve receives its blood supply primarily from branches of the external carotid artery.
Visual acuity should be tested with Ishihara plates.
fact: The optic nerve is surrounded by cranial meninges. It passes through the optic canal, is sensory, and visual acuity is assessed with a Snellen chart rather than Ishihara plates.
mnemonic: II carries meninges and vision; Snellen sees acuity, Ishihara sees colour.
finding: Source page displays meningeal investment as correct.

stem: The glossopharyngeal nerve exits the skull through the:
fact: The glossopharyngeal nerve exits the skull through the jugular foramen.
mnemonic: IX, X, and XI travel through the jugular foramen.
finding: Source page displays jugular foramen as correct.

stem: Which of the following nerves is the efferent pathway of the corneal blink reflex:
fact: The facial nerve is the efferent limb of the corneal blink reflex; V1 is the afferent limb.
mnemonic: V1 feels the cornea; VII closes the lids.
finding: Source page displays facial nerve as correct.

stem: A 64 year old man has sustained a penetrating injury to the submandibular triangle. On examination, his tongue is weak and when protruded deviates to the left. Which of the following nerves has most likely been injured:
fact: An ipsilateral hypoglossal LMN injury causes the tongue to deviate toward the weak side on protrusion; left deviation indicates left CN XII injury.
mnemonic: XII points toward the weak side.
finding: Source page displays left hypoglossal nerve as correct.

stem: The inferior alveolar nerve supplies all of the following EXCEPT for the:
options: Anterior belly of the digastric muscle
Sensation from skin over the chin
fact: The inferior alveolar nerve supplies lower teeth and chin sensation and gives the mylohyoid branch; tensor veli palatini is not supplied by it.
mnemonic: Inferior alveolar supplies lower teeth, chin, and mylohyoid; tensor veli palatini is the exception.
finding: Source page displays tensor veli palatini as the exception.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a typical feature of an abducens nerve palsy:
fact: CN VI palsy causes a convergent squint, horizontal diplopia, an adducted eye, and loss of abduction; inability to look up is not typical.
mnemonic: VI cannot look laterally; vertical upgaze is not its function.
finding: Source page displays inability to look up as not typical.
